pattern-selector.why: the design was chosen on purpose: one plan mode with a declarative schema table over one validator per skill, and a structural ADR pre-check over shelling to check_adr, to keep the plan check off bash.
pattern-selector.what: added the plan mode to check-task-plan.mjs (SKILL_TO_RECORD + a validateRecord schema table, validateAdr as a fast pre-check), recorded in ADR-0099 with the options and the rejected ones.
quotes: the structure that fits the forces this system will actually face, chosen on purpose

architectural-decision-records.why: the decision (a plan step that requires each applicable skill's planning record, complete, before a source edit) is recorded in the same change.
architectural-decision-records.what: added docs/adr/0099-planning-record-validators.md (context, three options, decision, consequences with honest limits) and a CHANGELOG entry.
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the sixteen step-3 behaviors (edit-before-plan-held, each planning record's happy and failing cases) are enumerated as scenarios, stored, logged, and run on the harness.
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: added the Step-3 rule with sixteen scenarios (one @audience:operator) to skills-formula, with step defs driving the real plan validator, regenerated the datastore, and appended the coverage log.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment.

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: the plan validator is proven at the lowest layer that can catch the bug: unit tests that spawn the real validator over fixtures.
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: added plan tests to test/check-task-plan.test.mjs (the happy set and a failing case per record type and per branch) and a step-3 deny to test/edit-gate.test.mjs.
quotes: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug

verifiable-quality-gates.why: the plan validator is a check, so every branch must be proven able to fail; the review found untested branches and they were given discriminating tests.
verifiable-quality-gates.what: added a negative test for each previously-unguarded branch (bdd-matrix, service-readiness, browser/usability verdicts, data-lifecycle, arch-standards, empty threats, the ADR section checks) plus a Nygard-ADR regression, so a surgical no-op of any branch flips a test.
quotes: test must FAIL when the check is replaced by a no-op

skeptical-audit.why: the plan validator enforces evidence discipline in code - a deletion, reversibility, alert-fires, UI, or load claim must reach observed or proven, not inferred - and the ADR records the limits.
skeptical-audit.what: evid() accepts only observed/proven for the evidence-bearing records; ADR-0099 names the limits (the schema proves presence and evidence state, not that the plan is sound; cited measurement/scenario names are unverified here).
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: the validator parses an untrusted plans file and resolves an ADR path, and it encodes the OWASP threat-modeling flow (each threat maps to a cheat sheet, a control, and a @security scenario).
owasp-secure-coding-bdd.what: the threat-model schema rejects a threat with no control and a control with no @security scenario (not-assessed, never a pass); plans input is parsed as JSON never eval'd; skill names from the selection pass isSafeName before any path join; the ADR pre-check rejects a dead-link confirmation file.
quotes: Each per-sheet file states the real attack the control stops

judge-arch.why: a fresh-context review ran on the diff before this receipt; it raised two medium findings, both fixed and pinned, and is recorded in the arch-review log.
judge-arch.what: dispatched the four-questions review to a general-purpose subagent; fixed the Nygard-ADR false-rejection (proven against the repo's own ADR 0001) and added the missing discriminating tests, plus a dead-code removal and an honest-limit note; recorded in docs/arch-reviews/log.jsonl.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: this change handles no personal or regulated data; its Definition of done (data class, retention basis, deletion observed/proven) is ENCODED as the data-lifecycle plan-record schema, not applied to a live data surface here.

release-deployment-safety.why: no deploy, migration, or rollout in this change; its Definition of done (reversibility observed/proven) is encoded as the reversibility plan-record schema, not applied to a live deployment here.

sre-operational-readiness.why: no running service or endpoint in this change; its Definition of done (SLIs, alerts, runbook, alert-fires observed/proven) is encoded as the service-readiness plan-record schema, not applied to a live service here.

universal-accessibility-wcag.why: no UI in this change; the a11y verdict requirement is encoded as a plan-record schema, not applied to a rendered surface here.

universal-browser-device-support.why: no browser- or device-facing code; the browser/device verdict requirement is encoded as a plan-record schema, not applied to a rendered surface here.

usability-ux-universal-design.why: no user-facing UI; the usability verdict requirement is encoded as a plan-record schema, and the validator's developer-facing messages follow the repo's checker-message style.

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: no new system or data architecture, schema, service, or scaling surface; its Definition of done is encoded as the arch-standards plan-record schema, and the boundary/ownership review is carried by judge-arch.

arch-encode.why: no new greppable arch-gate rule; the enforcement is a runtime validator plus discriminating tests, not a static lint over source.
